postureNote: Start with feet flat and the seat fully lowered. A high seat can force you to perch instead of using the backrest.
deskHighlight: Prioritize the lowest usable desktop setting and measure any keyboard surface with its mat installed.
chairHighlight: Start with a low cylinder and a short seat pan. Check the seat front clears the backs of both knees.

postureNote: Sit back before checking your feet. Sliding forward to reach the floor changes the effective seat depth.
deskHighlight: Measure whether a low keyboard tray can lower both keyboard and mouse while leaving knee space.
chairHighlight: Check the advertised cylinder configuration and measure seat height at its lowest loaded position.

postureNote: Check whether reaching your keyboard lifts your shoulders after you set the chair low enough to support your feet.
deskHighlight: A low sit-stand frame can be more useful than a higher frame with a large travel range.
chairHighlight: Check the fixed pan against your actual thigh length. A compact size label alone cannot establish fit.

postureNote: Set seat depth before moving the armrests. You should be able to use the backrest with space behind the knees.
deskHighlight: Compare the work surface minimum including the top thickness and any keyboard tray hardware.
chairHighlight: Look for a shallow functional pan and test whether the armrests lower enough to let you pull in.

postureNote: A change in footwear can change where your feet rest and where your elbows meet the desk.
deskHighlight: Check the lowest working keyboard height barefoot and in your usual indoor shoes.
chairHighlight: Test both the low-cylinder range and depth adjustment. Ensure a footrest would leave the knees clear.

postureNote: Keep the mouse beside the keyboard while checking elbow height. Reaching sideways can raise one shoulder.
deskHighlight: Allow room for both input devices on any lowered surface. Measure the mouse surface at the same height.
chairHighlight: Try a small depth adjustment while keeping full back contact and avoiding pressure behind the knees.

postureNote: Check seat fit with the chair in the upright position and again in your normal working recline.
deskHighlight: A center drawer or deep apron can reduce usable knee space even when desktop height looks right.
chairHighlight: Check how far the chair rolls in with its arms lowered and your feet still flat.

postureNote: Set your usual shoe allowance before choosing the first desk preset. Compare it with your barefoot setting.
deskHighlight: Confirm the frame covers both elbow targets with the actual desktop installed.
chairHighlight: Look for a cylinder range that covers your seated target with room to adjust in either direction.

postureNote: Keep your elbows close while testing keyboard reach. Moving the monitor forward should not pull the keyboard away.
deskHighlight: With a shallow top, measure from your eyes to the screen face and allow movement at the monitor mount.
chairHighlight: Compare the usable seat range while seated against the manufacturer figure for the exact cylinder.

postureNote: Use your measured seat depth if your leg proportions differ from the height-based estimate.
deskHighlight: Check the desk reaches your seated keyboard height without trapping your thighs beneath a controller or cable tray.
chairHighlight: Compare the published functional depth on adjustable chairs with the usable depth of a fixed-pan model.

postureNote: For an average-height starting profile, check elbow and eye height separately. Torso and leg proportions still matter.
deskHighlight: Start by checking the low end of an adjustable desk range before comparing advertised maximums.
chairHighlight: Test more than one fixed shell if your depth estimate falls near a sizing cutoff.

postureNote: Reset seat height after changing seat depth. Your contact with the backrest can shift with the slider setting.
deskHighlight: Compare the seated target against the keyboard surface on a fixed desk, including a thick keyboard if you use one.
chairHighlight: Aim for supported thighs and room behind the knees. Verify the pan can reach your setting without using the end stop.

postureNote: Check your seated line of sight while looking straight ahead with your head level and your back supported.
deskHighlight: Choose a frame that reaches both positions with equipment loaded, then set the screen separately.
chairHighlight: Try the chair with armrests adjusted low enough that your elbows can rest close to your sides.

postureNote: Practice switching posture without adjusting your chair just to reach the worktop. Let the desk move to meet your elbows.
deskHighlight: Measure the standing surface with relaxed shoulders. Check the monitor cable has slack at the highest preset.
chairHighlight: Compare the seat-depth range to the space you need behind the knees in both upright and supported recline.

postureNote: Check under-desk room while moving your feet and shifting position. A static knee check can miss frame obstructions.
deskHighlight: Measure floor-to-obstruction at the crossbar, drawer or controller, as well as floor-to-top.
chairHighlight: Confirm that enough thigh is supported when seated back, and check where lumbar support contacts your back.

postureNote: A longer thigh may need a deeper pan even if a standard cylinder reaches the right seat height.
deskHighlight: Check desktop maximum at your standing keyboard position with the desk feet leveled.
chairHighlight: Evaluate deep seat settings and backrest height separately. Keep clearance behind the knee.

postureNote: Check desk height standing in your usual shoes with arms relaxed. Shoulder shrugging can hide a worktop that is too high.
deskHighlight: Measure the standing target before choosing a frame and confirm the monitor can rise independently.
chairHighlight: Compare standard and tall cylinders by their actual ranges and check that the lowest setting remains usable.

postureNote: Check the seated and standing views of the same display. A stand that fits one position may need resetting in the other.
deskHighlight: Confirm both desktop travel and under-top knee clearance, especially around a front apron or tray.
chairHighlight: Verify seat depth and cylinder height independently. A high cylinder cannot compensate for a short pan.

postureNote: Check that your thighs clear the desk while rolling in and that you can use the backrest without perching.
deskHighlight: At the standing end of the range, raise the desk with the full load and check cables and frame movement.
chairHighlight: Try a deeper pan with enough room behind the knees. Check armrest and backrest travel for your torso.

postureNote: Measure your actual standing elbow height. A height-only estimate can miss a long or short torso.
deskHighlight: Compare the maximum with the top and leveling feet installed. Check monitor lift before buying a frame.
chairHighlight: Check the chair’s deep-pan setting and tall cylinder separately. Test the seated desk clearance before ordering.
